task.description:
FINAL RE-GATE of the ISS-0440 design (rework 2, commit b4ed0a41). You have failed this design twice, both times correctly, and the second failure exposed a repo-wide gap now filed as ISS-0441. Item 2 (the --dir override and AC1 demonstration mechanics) PASSED at the last gate and is SETTLED. This re-gate has exactly two questions plus a scope check.

1. IS THE THREE-TIER RESTATEMENT COMPLETE AND TRUE? CODE-DESIGNER rewrote sections 1 and 3.5 around: Tier 1 CI runs unconditionally (structural); Tier 2 a violation is therefore always detected and recorded (structural, follows from Tier 1); Tier 3 whether detection blocks the merge is PROCEDURAL, since no branch protection exists and PR #848 is a live counterexample. It reports independently re-verifying both facts, correcting AC1's framing, and finding one additional leftover Tier-3-strength sentence in 1.2 that had survived rework 1. ORCH grepped: surviving 'impossible to merge' strings are the design quoting the withdrawn claim (48, 488), affirming the true half (495), supplying the corrected sentence (539), and referencing the framing (847).
   VERIFY: (i) no section still argues from the withdrawn premise -- check 1.2's closing paragraph specifically, since that is where a leftover already hid once; (ii) Tier 2's claim is itself true -- does a violation REALLY get detected every time CI runs? Consider whether any path skips the linter within a CI run that does execute (e.g. an earlier alias step failing first and short-circuiting `mix letflow.check` before lint_handoffs is reached -- read mix.exs's alias ordering: lint_handoffs sits AFTER check_toolchain, check_requirements_registration and check_deferral_staleness, so if one of THOSE fails, does lint_handoffs still run?). If an earlier step can short-circuit it, Tier 2 is 'detected whenever CI reaches the linter', not 'always detected', and the design should say so. This is the same class of second-order overclaim you have now caught twice -- it is the last place it could hide.

2. ARE THE --dir GUARDS ADEQUATE? New section 2.1a specifies both a hard refusal when an explicitly-supplied --dir discovers zero files, AND an unconditional banner naming the scanned directory on every run including the default path. Judge whether the pair is sufficient and whether the banner is genuinely unmissable as specified. Separately, the design DECLINES to restrict --autofix against the real corpus, arguing that restricting it would reintroduce the 'agent must remember the safe flags' failure mode this design exists to eliminate, and would block a legitimate local-fix use case; it names the closed mapping, status-field-only scope, and per-file reporting as what makes it acceptable. Judge that reasoning. An unrestricted mass-rewrite path on a hard CI gate is a real risk, but so is a safety mechanism that depends on remembering a flag -- decide which argument wins here and say why. Either verdict is defensible if reasoned.

3. SCOPE CHECK. Confirm via git diff (b4ed0a41 against its parent) that rework 2 is confined to the three-tier restatement, the new 2.1a, the new 6.4, AC1's framing correction and the 1.2 leftover -- and that nothing settled moved: 2.1's --dir threading, resolve_dir/1's default, the byte-identical no-flag path, section 5's demonstration steps, the inside-handoffs/ rejection, both mechanisms' shapes, the four-option verdicts, the hook rejection, AC3/AC4/AC5, and the corrected 1900-file corpus figure. A rework that silently altered a settled element is itself a FAIL.

BIAS TOWARD CLOSING -- and read this carefully, because it is the last rework available. rework_count is 2 of max 3. A FAIL here leaves ONE attempt before ORCH must escalate per ORCHESTRATOR.md. The design's remaining defect class is descriptive accuracy, not mechanism. If the tiers are honest and the guards reasoned, PASS -- do not hold the gate for wording you would have phrased differently, and do not manufacture a third-order objection to be thorough. If you genuinely must FAIL, give the EXACT sentences required so rework 3 is a mechanical edit.

Do not edit lib/ or test/. Complete the handoff with per-item verdicts and a clear PASS/FAIL; on PASS route to ELIXIR-DEV. Commit to branch feature/WF03-ISS0440-20260903.

result.summary: FAIL. Final re-gate after rework 2 (design commit b4ed0a41). Independently verified the short-circuit finding ORCH reported at the Mix source level, not just by reproducing the empirical test -- and it holds, which makes Tier 2 as currently worded false. Items 2 and 3 are otherwise clean and are not what fails this gate.  ITEM 1(i) -- no leftover independent overclaim found. Re-read section 1.2's closing paragraph specifically, since that is where a leftover hid once before. It reads: Mechanism B does not, on its own, deliver Tier 1/2's unconditional-detection guarantee -- that is Mechanism A's alone (section 1.1), neither mechanism reaches Tier 3. This is a POINTER to section 1's Tier 2 definition, not an independent restatement of a claim -- it does not re-assert unconditional detection in its own words, it cites section 1's definition of that guarantee. So it carries no separate defect requiring its own edit; it will read correctly once Tier 2 itself is corrected (see 1(ii) below), and requires no additional change beyond that. Grepped the full document for impossible-to-merge / always-detected / structurally phrasing (all matches) and confirmed every remaining instance is either quoting the withdrawn rework-0/1 claims for contrast, or correctly scoped to the Tier framework -- no section argues from the withdrawn two-tier premise.  ITEM 1(ii) -- FAIL. Tier 2 (section 1, the second bullet) reads: a violation is therefore always DETECTED and RECORDED, Structural, verified -- this follows mechanically from Tier 1 and adds no further assumption. Independently verified this is false, going past ORCH's empirical reproduction to the Mix source itself: read the installed Elixir/Mix source at lib/mix/lib/mix/task.ex's run_alias/6 (private function, roughly lines 568-604) directly. It recurses through an alias's string list unconditionally calling do_run/run_task on each entry -- there is no branch anywhere in run_alias that inspects the previous step's result before continuing (confirmed: none of its five clauses reads or conditions on the underscore-prefixed res argument it receives). The short-circuit is not a result-check; it is that Mix.raise/1 raises a real exception, and the only rescue clause in the whole run/run_task/run_alias chain (task.ex, around line 502) is scoped narrowly to OptionParser.ParseError, re-raising it as a different Mix.raise -- a Mix.Error raised directly by an earlier alias entry is NOT caught anywhere in this path and unwinds the whole mix letflow.check invocation before run_alias's next recursive call (the one that would run letflow.lint_handoffs) is ever reached. Confirmed all three of mix.exs's earlier alias entries (letflow.check_toolchain, letflow.check_requirements_registration, letflow.check_deferral_staleness -- positions 1-3, ahead of letflow.lint_handoffs at position 4) call Mix.raise on failure (grep-confirmed in each task's own source). Independently reproduced the qualitative outcome too: mix do cmd exit 1 plus letflow.lint_handoffs aborts with a stacktrace and produces zero lint_handoffs output in the transcript, matching ORCH's reported result (the exact error differs by platform -- this Windows host has no exit executable reachable via System.cmd, so the abort comes from an enoent error rather than a literal exit code 1, but the load-bearing property, that letflow.lint_handoffs never runs and produces no output, is identical). So Tier 2's claim that it follows mechanically from Tier 1 and adds no further assumption is the false part: it silently assumes CI reaches the fourth alias entry, which is not guaranteed by Tier 1 firing -- Tier 1 (CI runs, unconditionally) is true and unaffected, but Tier 2 as worded overclaims one layer further than Tier 1 licenses. This is material, not a wording preference: it is the third consecutive layer (section 1.3/Mechanism B in rework 0, Tier 3 merge-blocking in rework 1, now Tier 2 detection in rework 2) at which an unconditional or structural claim has turned out conditional on request, and it sits at the design's own last remaining claim to unconditional strength, in a design whose entire stated purpose is not to overclaim. Against the it-still-surfaces-a-problem-later counter-argument: that is true and worth keeping in the corrected text, but it changes what Tier 2 guarantees (same-run detection of THIS violation vs. eventual awareness that SOME check failed) rather than making the current wording accurate -- a reader who takes always detected and recorded in the CI run's own log at face value would be wrong exactly when an earlier check task file has its own defect, which is a real, non-hypothetical class of failure this repo's own alias ordering can produce.  REQUIRED FIX, exact sentences, so rework 3 is mechanical: in section 1's Tier 2 bullet, after the sentence ending adds no further assumption, insert a new sentence stating this assumes the CI run actually reaches letflow.lint_handoffs -- it sits fourth in mix.exs's letflow.check alias, after letflow.check_toolchain, letflow.check_requirements_registration and letflow.check_deferral_staleness, each of which calls Mix.raise on its own failure and, per Mix's alias-running semantics (a raised Mix.Error is not rescued anywhere in the alias chain), aborts the whole invocation before any later entry runs -- so Tier 2's guarantee is that a violation is always detected and recorded whenever CI reaches the linter, which happens unless an earlier alias entry fails first, in which case that earlier failure still fails the same CI run (Tier 1 still holds: the job goes red) but H1's own check is not what is reported that run. Then update the two downstream restatements of Tier 2 at section 3.5 (the always-detected-and-recorded / CI's-own-output-or-rollup sentences) and AC1 (the check-always-runs-and-a-violation-is-always-detected-and-recorded-in-CI's-output sentence) to the same qualified form, or to a short cross-reference back to section 1's corrected text rather than repeating the unqualified claim a second and third time -- restating it verbatim in three places is what let the rework-1 fix miss one of its own echoes before, per section 1.2's pointer pattern which handled this correctly this round. Section 6.4 should also get one clause noting the Tier 2 qualifier does not change the recommended branch-protection follow-up, since branch protection requiring the same alias job to pass would close both the Tier 2 ordering gap and the Tier 3 merge-blocking gap at once via the same repo-administration action.  ITEM 2 -- PASS. Section 2.1a's two guards (hard Mix.raise refusal when an explicitly supplied --dir discovers zero files; an unconditional banner naming the scanned directory and file count on every invocation including the default path) are both present and their joint necessity is explicitly reasoned -- the empty-scope guard alone would not catch a non-empty-but-wrong directory, and the banner alone would not hard-stop a genuinely empty misdirected scan; together neither hazard passes unlabelled. The empty-default-directory carve-out (default @handoffs_dir with zero files is NOT the misuse case, since a legitimately empty handoffs/ is a pre-existing edge case of handoff_files/1 itself, not a --dir-introduced one) is a sound, explicitly reasoned distinction, not a loophole. On the --autofix-unrestricted question: the design's argument -- restricting --autofix to non-default directories would reintroduce the exact agent-must-remember-the-safe-flag failure mode this whole design exists to eliminate, and would block the legitimate local-fix use case -- is sound and wins over the restrict-it alternative. The three concrete safety properties it cites (closed 3-value map touching only the status field; every fix reported by path and old-to-new value, never silent; verified no-op against today's real corpus, stated as a fact about today's state rather than a property of the flag, correctly not conflating the two) genuinely bound the risk rather than merely asserting safety. This is a reasoned, defensible call under the task's own either-verdict-is-defensible-if-reasoned standard. No defect found on this item.  ITEM 3 (SCOPE CHECK) -- PASS. git diff between b4ed0a41's parent and b4ed0a41's header-level hunks show exactly the claimed changes: section 1/1.1 rewritten into the three-tier framing, new section 2.1a, section 3.5 corrected, new section 6.4. Directly diffed the settled sections byte for byte between the rework-1 and rework-2 versions of the file (section 4's four-option verdicts including the hook rejection; section 5's six numbered AC1 demonstration steps; AC3/AC4/AC5) and all three are IDENTICAL, zero diff lines -- nothing settled silently moved. resolve_dir/1's default-preserving contract, the byte-identical no-flag path, and the 1900-file corpus figure are referenced only in new additions (section 2.1a citing them), never altered in their original locations.  VERDICT: FAIL. One BLOCKER (Item 1(ii), Tier 2's unqualified always-detected claim is false given Mix's alias short-circuit semantics, independently confirmed at the Mix source level). Items 1(i), 2, and 3 all pass cleanly. This is the exact defect class already caught twice, now at its last hiding place; per the rework dispatch's own framing this is a one-sentence-plus-two-cross-reference-updates fix, not a redesign, so rework 3 should be mechanical.

issues.description: Item 1(ii): design section 1's Tier 2 bullet claims a violation is always DETECTED and RECORDED, and that this follows mechanically from Tier 1 and adds no further assumption. Verified false at the Mix source level (not just by reproducing ORCH's empirical test): the installed Elixir/Mix source at lib/mix/lib/mix/task.ex's run_alias/6 recurses through an alias's string list with no check of the previous step's result before continuing, and the only rescue in the whole run/run_task/run_alias chain is scoped narrowly to OptionParser.ParseError -- a Mix.Error raised by an earlier alias entry (confirmed: letflow.check_toolchain, letflow.check_requirements_registration and letflow.check_deferral_staleness, positions 1-3 ahead of letflow.lint_handoffs at position 4 in mix.exs's letflow.check alias, all three call Mix.raise on failure) is not caught anywhere and unwinds the whole mix letflow.check invocation before letflow.lint_handoffs is ever reached. Independently reproduced the qualitative outcome (mix do cmd exit 1 plus letflow.lint_handoffs aborts with a stacktrace, zero lint_handoffs output). Tier 1 (CI runs unconditionally) remains true; Tier 2 as worded silently assumes CI reaches the fourth alias entry, which Tier 1 does not license. This is the third consecutive layer at which an unconditional or structural claim has needed a scope qualifier, in a design whose stated purpose is not to overclaim -- material, not a wording preference. Rework: in section 1's Tier 2 bullet, after the no-further-assumption sentence, add a qualifying sentence stating this assumes CI reaches the linter, naming the three earlier alias entries and their Mix.raise-on-failure behaviour, and stating the corrected guarantee as always detected and recorded whenever CI reaches the linter, which happens unless an earlier alias entry fails first -- in which case Tier 1 still holds (the job goes red) but H1's own check is not what is reported that run. Then update section 3.5's and AC1's own restatements of the same claim to match -- either the same qualified wording or a short pointer back to section 1's corrected text rather than repeating the unqualified claim verbatim a second and third time. Section 6.4 should note the branch-protection follow-up would close this ordering gap too, via the same repo-administration action, since it is the same underlying question (does a problem detected anywhere in the job actually block the merge or get reported this run).
